name: Brown & Brown, Inc.

profile.description: Brown & Brown is the world's fifth-largest insurance broker, providing property & casualty, employee benefits, and specialty risk solutions through its Retail, Specialty Distribution (programs and wholesale), and Services segments. FY2025 revenue rose 22.5% to $5.76B, lifting BRO to No. 5 among global brokers after the Accession acquisition [4][5]. Q3 2026 revenue was $1.725B (+7.4% YoY), but organic growth was only 1.2% as softer pricing in catastrophe property weighed on results [1][2]. CEO J. Powell Brown positions AI as a productivity tool, targeting 25% submission automation without job cuts [3].

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): The Accession acquisition was a scale-changing launch into a new tier — FY2025 revenue rose 22.5% to $5.76B and moved BRO up to No. 5 among the world's largest brokers [4][5]; 5-year revenue CAGR is 17.2% ($2.61B in 2020 to $5.76B in 2025) [6]. AI Deployment (1/2): AI agents are already automating portions of the end-to-end submission process in Specialty Distribution, with a stated 25% submission-automation target, but no quantified savings or revenue have been reported yet [3]. Market Share (1/2): A top-5 global broker, but organic growth of 0.3% for the first nine months of 2026 versus 4.6% a year earlier shows it is not currently a share gainer [1][2]. Product Pipeline (0/2): No named next-generation offerings with launch dates and revenue visibility were found. R&D Intensity (0/1): FMP data shows no reported R&D expense; brokerage does not invest in R&D as a percentage of revenue [6].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): BRO's 'Focused on Forever' positioning and CEO Powell Brown's line that 'AI does not disintermediate trust' — the business 'is built on trust and good advice' — describe what BRO does and how, but not a distinctive future it is working toward [3]. Community Impact (0/2): The search surfaced only the self-reported, SASB-aligned 2025 Global Impact Report (no external assurance); no specific foundation programs or dollar amounts were found [7]. Employee Retention (0/2): No turnover or tenure data was found; the pledge to automate without job cuts is a positive signal but not retention evidence [3]. Insider Buying (1/2): Insiders made three purchases totaling 5,678 shares (~$456K) over the prior twelve months, including Director H. Palmer Proctor Jr.'s 2,000-share purchase (~$114K) in May 2026, and insiders own 13.1% of the company — supportive but small and director-led rather than CEO-led [7].

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on the Growth framework (weighted sum 8.314 of 10 = 8/10) [6][8]. Strengths: D/E of 64.2% beats the 70% target (1.0), the 5-year revenue CAGR of 17.2% (2× weight) exceeds the 10% target (1.0), and forward P/E of 14.6x is well under 20x (1.0). Q3 2026 revenue growth of 7.4% scores 0.91 and profit margin of 17.9% scores 0.89 [1]. Drags: ROE of 9.8% (2× weight) scores only 0.65 as Accession goodwill swelled the equity base, and the PEG of 1.80 (2× weight) scores 0.60. Liquidity is ample at ~$157M of average daily dollar volume (2.25M shares x $69.76) [8].

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (7/9): Mizuho concluded that brokers focused on middle-market and large accounts face a 'low disruption threat' from AI, and Barclays argued the market has overreacted to AI disruption fears in the broker sector [3]. CEO Powell Brown argues AI will not displace brokers on complex middle-market and specialty risks because trust and advisory expertise remain central to buying insurance [3]. Residual exposure exists in small-commercial and personal lines where carrier-direct and AI-enabled distribution can disintermediate simple placements, which keeps BRO out of the 8–9 'immune' tier. AI Opportunity (0/1): AI agents automate parts of submission processing, but no AI-attributable revenue or quantified savings has been disclosed [3].

infinite_game.summary: Through Sinek's lens, Brown & Brown is a durable, family-led franchise whose 'Focused on Forever' language and long CEO tenure point toward the infinite game, but its growth engine is now almost entirely acquisition-driven: Q3 2026 revenue grew 7.4% while organic growth was just 1.2%, and nine-month organic growth was 0.3% [1][2]. The pledge to deploy AI without job cuts is a genuine Circle of Safety signal [3]. The question for an infinite player is whether BRO can grow the book it already owns rather than buying revenue.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): 'Focused on Forever' and the CEO's insistence that the business is 'built on trust and good advice' form a distinctive, relationship-centered purpose that leadership references publicly [3]. It shapes integration of acquired agencies, but it describes how BRO serves rather than a future state it is pursuing, so it falls short of a validated Just Cause.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Management's commitment that AI automation (25% of submissions targeted) will not trigger job cuts supports psychological safety during change [3]. Insiders own 13.1% of the company, aligning leaders with employees and owners [7]. No retention or tenure data was found to justify the top score.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): The search found no management commentary framing competitors such as Marsh, Aon, or Gallagher as benchmarks to learn from; analyst commentary instead highlights BRO's organic growth lagging peers [4]. No evidence for the point was found.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): BRO has evolved from a regional agency into a top-5 global broker and is now rewiring workflows with AI agents in Specialty Distribution [3][4]. These are evolutionary changes within insurance distribution, not a reinvention of the business model.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Leadership made a large, capital-intensive bet with Accession (revenue +22.5% in FY2025) and is investing in AI automation while explicitly ruling out job cuts — a choice that forgoes easy near-term cost savings [3][5]. However, there is no evidence of exiting profitable but misaligned businesses, and the stock-acquisition model can mask weak organic growth.

investment_thesis: Brown & Brown trades at 14.6x forward earnings with a conservative balance sheet (D/E 64%) for a company that has compounded revenue at 17.2% annually since 2020 and reached $5.76B in FY2025, now the No. 5 global broker [5][6][8]. Q3 2026 revenue rose 7.4% to $1.725B and net income rose 5.7% to $240M, with adjusted EPS up 1.9% to $1.07 [1]. Insurance brokerage is one of the more AI-insulated corners of financial services — Mizuho sees a 'low disruption threat' for middle-market brokers — and BRO is using AI agents to automate up to 25% of submissions without job cuts, which could lift margins over time [3]. The dividend was raised 9% to $0.18 quarterly in October 2026 [9].
thesis_continued: The bear case is organic stagnation in a softening pricing cycle. Organic revenue grew only 1.2% in Q3 2026 after a 0.7% decline in Q2, and nine-month organic growth was 0.3% versus 4.6% a year earlier, as catastrophe-property rates softened [1][2]. Adjusted EBITDAC margin fell to 34.6% from 36.6%, and diluted EPS declined 1.5% to $0.67 [1]. ROE has fallen to 9.8% as acquisition goodwill expanded equity, and the PEG of 1.8 implies the market is not cheap relative to growth [8]. If the P&C market softens further, commission revenue will fall regardless of AI productivity gains.
key_catalysts: AI submission automation: management targets 25% automation of submissions in Specialty Distribution without job cuts, which could restore EBITDAC margins from 34.6% toward the prior-year 36.6% [1][3]

Accession integration and cross-selling: full integration of the business that lifted FY2025 revenue 22.5% to $5.76B should produce cost synergies and help organic growth recover from the 0.3% nine-month pace [2][5]
Dividend growth and capital return: the October 2026 increase to $0.18 per quarter (+9%) continues a 12.3% five-year dividend CAGR with a payout ratio near 21% [8][9]
key_risks: Soft-market pricing: catastrophe-property rate declines already cut organic growth to 1.2% in Q3 2026; a broader P&C softening would pressure commission revenue across Retail and Specialty Distribution [1][2]
Margin compression: adjusted EBITDAC margin fell 200bps to 34.6% in Q3 2026; continued compression would undermine the 14.6x forward multiple [1]
Acquisition dependence: with organic growth near zero, total growth relies on M&A, and ROE has already fallen to 9.8% as goodwill builds; overpaying for deals would further dilute returns [6][8]
